text: Add background embedding powered idea consolidation with human review for ambiguous cases
description: Periodically analyze the active idea graph using its embeddings to surface likely duplicates, missing connections, and conflicting ideas. Apply only high confidence, low risk cases automatically: merge clear restatements while preserving history and rewiring links; add a connection only when direction and support relationship are obvious; resolve conflicts only when the contradiction and authoritative resolution are explicit in the ideas. Queue uncertain or consequential cases for the user, with evidence and proposed actions. Start review with five most interesting cases, one at a time, and learn from user decisions. Never infer a conflict resolution from similarity alone. Embedding input should remain grounded in the idea’s own text, description, and tags; do not append parent or supported-idea content, since an arbitrary claimed support link could then move another idea embedding. Treat graph relationships as separate evidence, not as embedding text.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: The session should surface candidate duplicates, missing links, and conflicts for human review as new aims are recorded.
An on-demand LLM link proposal, judged by the human, finds non-obvious contributions that embeddings miss, while keeping link decisions human.

status.comment: The on-demand part exists: the consolidate prompt (f0c0ffe0) runs duplicates, structure and status checks and queues decisions for the human. This idea asks for more: a periodic background run that merges clear restatements automatically. That conflicts with the consolidate rule that merges stay human decisions, and calibration showed most high-cosine pairs are intended parent-child splits. Question for Felix: allow automatic merges of exact restatements in a background run, or keep merges human-only and cancel the background part?
